title: Tenant-triggered data retirement and verification playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Implement a tenant-driven data retirement flow that lets a customer request a scoped 'retirement' (right-to-be-forgotten) operation for a tenant or set of tenant-scoped entities, verifies purge completion across storage backends, and emits a chronological audit trail that customers can consume. This ticket covers the product playbook, API surface, required orchestration primitives in the control plane, and the evidence/verification export format.

Background: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions require both the ability to request data removal and a machine-readable, time-stamped proof that removal completed across pipelines (object stores, DB shards, analytics exports, backups). Existing Redwood tickets focus on purge engines and regional deletions; this playbook ties tenant initiation, retention-window awareness, and cross-backend reconciliation together so we can support self-serve RTBF for Dedicated/Private and hosted customers.

Goals:
- Define the tenant-facing API and console flow for initiating a retirement request (scope selection, preview, dry-run).
- Define control plane orchestration steps (validate scope, schedule retire job respecting retention rules, issue retirement token, coordinate with storage adapters, reconcile results).
- Create a compact, chronological audit export format (jsonl) that includes: retirement_token, scoped_manifest, per-backend status, timestamps, operator signatures, and optional operator notes.
- Provide automated verification routines that re-check post-retirement manifests and surface any residual objects for manual remediation.
- Ensure export can be consumed by customers and used as evidence for compliance officers.

Non-goals: full legal certification, cross-tenant aggregation reporting, automatic compensation for third-party exports (handled by follow-up work).

Acceptance Criteria: (1) Console and API flows for tenant-triggered retirement exist and pass E2E test harness; (2) Orchestration emits retirement tokens and chronological audit export for every completed run; (3) Automated verification runner flags mismatches and creates a remediation todo for ops; (4) Documentation and quickstart for customers to download evidence and validate receipts.

Success metrics: percentage of retirement requests that complete within SLA (target 95% within 24h), mean time-to-detect residual objects (<6h), number of customer support tickets related to retirement evidence decreases after launch.

Risks/Assumptions: assumes storage adapters can perform idempotent object tombstone operations and report deterministically; backups/long-term archives may require separate legal handling (not completed by this scope).
